BURHAN:v2p129/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.claim: The Prophet supported his descriptions of Paradise with verses: unseen delights by 32:17, the promise to work by the verses of al-Layl, and the tree's long shade by 56:30.
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.anchor: منها حين ذكر ما أعد الله تعالى لأوليائه فى الجنة فقال فيها ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر

QASHANI:92:8-12/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:8-12/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:8-12/r1.claim: The miser chooses love and hoarding of wealth, relying on it instead of acquiring virtue, and is thereby veiled from God.
QASHANI:92:8-12/r1.anchor: آثر محبة المال وجمعه ومنعه واستغنى به عن كسب الفضيلة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.claim: Verses 8–10 describe the character and belief that lead a person to doom and Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.anchor: Mentioned in these verses are the character and ideology of a person which lead him to doom and to the pit of Hell.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.claim: Those who treat worldly life as ultimate are miserly, heedless of the Hereafter, and lack resolve for its reward; God lets them pursue their chosen way toward hardship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.anchor: They are misers and callously guard their wealth and have no fear of the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.claim: God leaves people without courage for virtue to their base desires; they may seem to progress smoothly until death, then face the steep hardship of 74:17.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.anchor: they reach the end of their lives

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r2.claim: The wealthy may credit their riches to their own intelligence, like Qārūn’s claim at 28:78; Islahi says the verse overturns this self-reliant capitalist mentality because all gain comes from God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r2.anchor: in the next is also from God

TUSTARI:92:8/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:8/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:92:8/r1.claim: Abu Jahl’s miserliness was withholding obedience to God and His Messenger, while his self-sufficiency was a show of needing neither.
TUSTARI:92:8/r1.anchor: أبو جهل بخل بطاعته لله ورسوله، واستغنى: أظهر من نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.claim: The surah explains which traits bring the success and failure just mentioned in the previous surah, then warns of the Fire and distinguishes those entering it from those spared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها ، ذكر هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149/r1.claim: The one who withholds does not spend wealth for good; a second reading says he withholds required actions, which Alusi finds unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149/r1.anchor: بما له فلم يبذله في سبيل الخير وقيل أي بخل بفعل ما أمر به

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149/r2.claim: He acts as though independent of God, or prefers worldly desires to the blessings of the afterlife; the latter reading contrasts with “and was God-conscious.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149/r2.anchor: أي وزهد فيما عنده عز وجل كأنه مستغن عنه سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r3.speaker: الإرشاد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r3.claim: Al-Irshad explains why giving and withholding open the two clauses: each is foundational for the later belief, piety, denial, or self-sufficiency.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r3.anchor: في الإرشاد لعل تصدير القسمين بالإعطاء والبخل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r8.speaker: ابن زيد وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r8.claim: Some identify the giver as Abu Bakr and the miser as Umayya ibn Khalaf; Ibn Abbas reports instead identify Abu Sufyan, while a report via al-Tusti names Abu Jahl. Alusi objects that Abu Sufyan became a firm Muslim; these are instances of the general wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r8.anchor: وقيل من أعطى أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه ومن بخل أمية بن خلف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r2.claim: The miser withholds good spending, seeks no reward from God, and denies the promised good; God prepares him for evil until he merits the Fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r2.anchor: {وكذب بالحسنى فسنيسره للعسرى} سنهيئه للشر بأن نجريه على يديه حتى يعمل بما لا يرضي الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.claim: In this story, the giver is Abu al-Dahdah, the promised good is reward, and the easier path is Paradise; the miser is the Ansari, who denies reward and is eased toward Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.anchor: {وأما من بخل واستغنى} يعني الأنصاري، {وكذب بالحسنى} يعني الثواب، {فسنيسره للعسرى} يعني النار.

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r1.claim: The other person withholds what was commanded and is satisfied with worldly desires instead of the next life’s bliss.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r1.anchor: { وأما من بخل } بما أمر به. { واستغنى } بشهوات الدنيا عن نعيم العقبى

BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.claim: The contrast concerns giving away wealth and hoarding it: the passage says the miser's wealth will not help him and describes the giver as giving wealth to purify himself.
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.anchor: وإنه لكذلك، الإعطاء للمال والبخل به، في آيتي الليل

BINTSHATI:v2p106/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r2.claim: Giving or withholding wealth concerns what should be spent for good and God's due to its rightful recipients through alms, charity, and generosity.
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r2.anchor: فيما يجب أن ينفق فيه المال من وجوه الخير، وأداء حق الله

BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.claim: The oath's night, daylight, and creation frame divergent earthly endeavors, then contrasting afterlife fates: the denier's fire and the pious giver's satisfaction.
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا النسق من البيان المعجز، يتم الربط بين المقسم به في أول السورة:

BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r4.claim: The miser withholds what was commanded or encouraged; istaghnā means seeking independence from people and from promised reward through vain assumptions.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r4.anchor: واستغنى } أي طلب الغنى عن الناس وعما وعد به من الثواب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r7.claim: The majestic plural signals how unlikely either path is: good is hard because surrounded by aversions, while reason and primordial nature warn against evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r7.anchor: وأشار بنون العظمة في كل من نجد الخير ونجد الشر إلى أن ارتكاب الإنسان لكل منهما في غاية البعد

NAHHAS:v5p241/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p241/r12.claim: On that interpretation, the miser withheld his alms and felt no need for his Lord's reward.
NAHHAS:v5p241/r12.anchor: على ذلك القول بخل بزكاته واستغنى عن ثواب ربه جل وعز

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.claim: He reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal for God; the verses contrast their efforts with those of Umayya and Ubayy, identify the good as the testimony of faith, and the hard path as Hell.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ وابن عساكر عن ابن مسعود

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.claim: Giving means giving from one's bounty and fearing God; the good promise is God's compensation, ease is good, and the opposite is withholding wealth, self-sufficiency, denial, and ease toward evil.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن جرير والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.claim: He said the giver pays God's due, avoids prohibitions, and believes God's promise; the miser withholds that due, feels self-sufficient, and denies the promise.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r9.claim: He also glossed the good as affirming that there is no god but God; the miser is one who withholds zakat despite having been enriched.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.claim: In a report through al-Kalbi and Abu Salih, the giver and God-fearing person is Abu Bakr, while the miser who feels self-sufficient and denies the good is Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن مردويه وابن عساكر في طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.claim: The Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Fire is written, but commanded people to act: each is made ready for the deeds of the saved or the wretched, then recited this passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وعبد بن حميد والبخاري ومسلم وأبو داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجة وابن مردويه وابن جرير عن علي بن أبي طالب

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.claim: Suraqa asked whether deeds were predetermined; the Prophet affirmed the decree but urged action, since each person is eased toward what he was created for, then recited the passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.anchor: وأخرج أحمد ومسلم وابن حبان والطبراني وابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas links the sura's revelation to a sale: a stingy palm owner deprived a poor household of fallen dates, then a believer traded forty palms for the tree and gave it to the family; the buyer received a promised palm in Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ان رجلا كان له نخل ومنها نخلة فرعها إلى دار رجل صالح فقير ذي عيال

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#3/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the miserly person as one who withholds his wealth and considers himself independent of his Lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#3/r3.anchor: قال عكرمة عن ابن عباس ، اي بخل بماله واستغنى عن ربه عز وجل

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the miser withholds wealth, relies on himself, denies God's replacement, and is eased toward evil.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.anchor: واما من بخل واستغنى قال : بخل بماله واستغنى عن ربه وكذب بالحسنى قال : الخلف من الله فسنيسره للعسرى قال : للشر من الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r5.claim: Qatadah says miserliness means withholding God's due and considering oneself independent of one's Lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r5.anchor: واما من بخل قال : بحق الله عليه واستغنى في نفسه عن ربه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r9.claim: The Prophet says angels call at every sunset for God to replace what spenders give and ruin what misers withhold; the report says these verses were revealed about that.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r9.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ما من يوم غربت فيه شمسه الا وبجنبتيها ملكان يناديان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r2.claim: The object of بخل is omitted because it means being stingy with wealth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r2.anchor: وكذلك فعل { بخل } لم يذكر متعلقه لأنه أريد به البخل بالمال .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r3.claim: استغنى opposes piety and means considering oneself independent of God's commands and call, relying instead on idols and one's people; its prefix may intensify the act or indicate seeking greater wealth through hoarding, both identifying the idolater.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r3.anchor: و { استغنى } جعل مقابلا ل { اتقى } فالمراد به الاستغناء عن امتثال أمر الله ودعوته لأن المصر على الكفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r2.claim: Giving and miserliness are named even though covered by piety and self-sufficiency to encourage Muslims to give; giving, piety, and affirmation mark believers, while their opposites mark idolaters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r2.anchor: وإنما خص الإعطاء بالذكر في قوله : { فأما من أعطى واتقى } مع شمول { اتقى } لمفاده ، وخص البخل بالذكر في قوله : { وأما من بخل واستغنى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.claim: The passage uses الجمع مع التقسيم and four antitheses: giving versus withholding, piety versus self-sufficiency, affirmation versus denial, and ease versus hardship.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p490#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p490#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p490#2/r11.claim: Miserliness extends beyond wealth to faith and other speech that religious law requires people to give.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p490#2/r11.anchor: وكذلك البخل المذكور بعد أن يكون بالإيمان وغيره من الأقوال التي حق الشريعة أن لا يبخل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r2.claim: If miserliness means withholding wealth, istaghna also concerns wealth and intensifies the blame; if it is broad, he claims independence from God and mercy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r2.anchor: ومن جعل بخل في المال خاصة جعل استغنى في المال أيضا لتعظم المذمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r3.claim: The subsequent question about wealth when he falls suggests that giving and miserliness here concern wealth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r3.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الإعطاء والبخل المذكورين إنما هما في المال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150/r1.claim: The miserly person is Umayya and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150/r1.anchor: قال ابن مسعود يعني ذلك أمية وأبي ابني خلف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150/r2.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150/r2.claim: Alternatively, the person is the owner of the palm tree.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150/r3.claim: He withholds spending on good works and charity; Qatāda specifies withholding God's due and acting as though he does not need God's reward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150/r3.anchor: بخل بالنفقة في الخير والصدقة وقال قتادة بحق الله عز وجل واستغنى عن ثواب الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ikrimah, glosses miserliness as withholding one's wealth and claiming independence from one's Lord.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أي بخل بماله، واستغنى عن ربه، عز وجل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r4.claim: Two angels flank each sunset, asking God to replace what a spender gives and destroy what a hoarder withholds; Abu al-Darda's report says the verses were revealed about this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r4.anchor: اللهم أعط منفقا خلفا، وأعط ممسكا تلفا". وأنزل الله في ذلك القرآن:

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r1.claim: استغنى can mean turning away from God's reward as if one did not need Him, and so failing to fear Him; or worldly pleasures can make one feel independent of Paradise's reward, opposite to God-consciousness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r1.anchor: { واستغنى } وزهد فيما عند الله كأنه مستغن عنه فلم يتقه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.claim: One report says these verses concern Abu Bakr and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.anchor: وقيل : نزلتا في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه ، وفي أبي سفيان بن حرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r29.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r29.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the miser who considers himself independent as Umayya and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r29.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : يعني بذلك أمية وأبيا ابني خلف .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r30.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r30.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan say the miser withholds his wealth, which will not last.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r30.anchor: بخل بماله الذي لا يبقى , قاله ابن عباس والحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r31.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r31.claim: Qatada says he withholds the right due to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r31.anchor: الثاني : بخل بحق الله تعالى , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r32.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r32.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r32.claim: Al-Hasan says the person considers himself independent through his wealth.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r33.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r33.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r33.claim: Ibn Abbas says he considers himself independent of his Lord.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r33.anchor: الثاني : عن ربه , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.speaker: أبو الدرداء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.claim: Qatada reports from Khulayd, from Abu al-Darda, that the Prophet said two angels call each sunrise for God to replace the spender's gift and ruin the hoarder's wealth, then recited these verses; no grading is stated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.anchor: يروي قتادة عن خليد عن أبي الدرداء أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( ما من يوم طلعت فيه شمسه إلا وملكان يناديان : اللهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#9/r1.claim: The miser withholds his wealth and considers himself independent of his Lord, so he does not fear Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#9/r1.anchor: ﴿ وأما من بخل ﴾ بماله ﴿ واستغنى ﴾ عن ربه فلم يتقه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#9/r2.claim: Alternatively, he is engrossed in worldly desires instead of the pleasures of the afterlife.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#9/r2.anchor: فلم يتقه أ واستغنى بشهوات الدنيا عن نعيم العقبى

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.speaker: علي عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.claim: At a funeral in Baqiʿ, the Prophet says each soul's destination is written, but people must act; each person is made ready for the work of the blessed or wretched, then he recites these verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.anchor: ما من نفس منفوسة إلا قد كتب مدخلها

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.speaker: علي عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhi's wording is graded hasan sahih; the Prophet repeats that everyone is made easy for the work for which they were created.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.anchor: بل اعملوا فكل ميسر أما من كان من أهل السعادة فإنه ييسر لعمل السعادة

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.speaker: غلامان شابان عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.claim: Two young men ask whether deeds follow prior decrees or begin anew; the Prophet says decrees, then tells them to act because each is enabled for the work assigned to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.anchor: «بل فيما جفت به الأقلام، وجرت به المقادير» قالا: ففيم العمل

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.speaker: الغلامان
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.claim: After hearing that each is made easy for the work for which he was created, the young men say they will strive and work.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r5.claim: The miser withholds his property and does not give anything good; the consequence is discussed in Aal ʿImran, while this passage says he ends in Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وأما من بخل واستغنى } أي ضن بما عنده، فلم يبذل خيرا.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r7.claim: He says the passage was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r8.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r8.claim: He says the man hoards wealth and considers himself independent of his Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r8.anchor: وعنه عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت في أمية بن خلف وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس: «وأما من بخل واستغنى» يقول: بخل بماله، واستغنى عن ربه.

QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r1.claim: The miser withholds self and wealth, claims no need for God or guidance, and denies the good creed; humanity’s diverse lives ultimately meet in two ranks.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r1.anchor: ومن بخل بنفسه وماله . واستغنى عن الله وهداه . وكذب بهذه الحسنى

QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r2.claim: Each rank has its own path in life and receives facilitation along that path.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r2.anchor: لكل منهما في هذه الحياة طريق

QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r3.claim: Withholding oneself and wealth, and rejecting God and His guidance, exposes a person to the greatest corruption they can bring upon themselves.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:8/r3.anchor: يبلغ أقصى ما يبلغه إنسان بنفسه من تعريضها للفساد

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.claim: The passage explains that the differing human paths end in praiseworthy or blameworthy outcomes, reward or punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.anchor: بين معنى اختلاف الأعمال فيما قلناه من العاقبة المحمودة والمذمومة

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet taught each person's destination is recorded, then urged action because everyone is eased toward what they were created for; he recited these verses.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.anchor: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib related that the Prophet said, “There is no one among you except that his place is registered

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r8.claim: Although “self-sufficient” is literal, “deems himself beyond need” conveys the negative illusion of independence from God.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r8.anchor: but beyond need better conveys the negative connotation of viewing oneself

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r9.claim: Miserliness toward those below and imagined independence from what is above invert the proper balance: obedience to God and generosity toward others.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r9.anchor: Being miserly toward those below one’s station and having the illusion of self-sufficiency in relation to what is above is an inversion of the proper balance

ASAD-NOTES:92:8#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:92:8#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:92:8#n5/r1.claim: Asad links the claim of self-sufficiency with 96:6-7.

TAB-FULL:v24p467/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p467/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p467/r1.claim: Al-Tabari contrasts the easier course of obedience prepared for the giver with the miser who withholds the bounty given by God and considers himself independent of his Lord.
TAB-FULL:v24p467/r1.anchor: وأما من بخل بالنفقة في سبيل الله، ومنع ما وهب الله له من فضله

TAB-FULL:v24p467/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p467/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p467/r2.claim: The miser withholds God's bounty from commanded uses and considers himself independent of his Lord, so he does not seek to obey Him or increase in what he was given.
TAB-FULL:v24p467/r2.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: وأما من بخل بالنفقة في سبيل الله، ومنع ما وهب الله له من فضله

TAB-FULL:v24p467/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p467/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p467/r3.claim: They describe the miser as withholding his wealth, surplus, or God's due, and living as if independent of the Lord.
TAB-FULL:v24p467/r3.anchor: وأما من بخل بحق الله عليه، واستغنى في نفسه

TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن علي
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.claim: When asked whether people should rely on their written destinies, the Prophet commands them to act: each person is made ready for his path, and he recites the two contrasting passages.

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن علي
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.claim: Several versions say each person's place in Paradise or Hell is written, yet people must act; each is facilitated toward the work for which they were created.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.anchor: لا اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن النزال بن سبرة
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.claim: A report says every soul's outcome is written; in response to an Arab's question the Prophet says God guides each person toward good or evil, with these verses cited.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.anchor: كل ميسر لما خلق له، فمن يرد الله به خيرا

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن سعد بن عبيدة وأبي عبد الرحمن السلمي
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.claim: When asked what work means if everything is decreed, the Prophet says to act because each person is facilitated for the easier or harder path.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.anchor: اعملوا فكل ميسر: سنيسره لليسرى، وسنيسره للعسرى

TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.claim: Asked whether people act for something already decided or begin something new, the Prophet answers that every worker is made ready for his work.

TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن بشير بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.claim: The Prophet says work follows what the pens and decrees have fixed, but people must still act; each is facilitated for the work for which they were created.
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.anchor: اعملوا، فكل عامل ميسر لعمله الذي خلق له

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.claim: The opposition between ease and hardship parallels 94:5–6, while the promise in 87:8 addresses the messenger.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Vgl. die Entgegensetzung von ʿusr und yusr in 94:5.6 sowie die wie 94:5.6 an den Verkünder gerichtete Verheißung 87:8

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.claim: Istaġnā is an antonym of ittaqā and appears near taqwā in 96:7; in 80:5 the positive counterpart is piety in 80:9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Das Verb wird hier offensichtlich als Antonym zu ittaqā (V. 5) gebraucht; auch in 96:7 steht istaġnā in der Nähe von taqwā

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r2.claim: The translation 'being self-sufficient' is preferable to Paret's 'acting arrogantly' so the three occurrences remain consistent.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Die Übersetzung „an sich selbst genug haben“ anstelle von „selbstherrlich auftreten“ (so Paret) empfiehlt sich, um alle drei Vorkommnisse konkordant übersetzen zu können

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.claim: The first antithesis pairs virtue and vice catalogues with promises of their eschatological outcomes; first-person plural marks these promises as God's speech and authorizes them alongside the oath.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.anchor: Diese Ankündigungen stehen in der ersten Person Plural, sind also eindeutig als Gottesrede markiert – ein Mittel literarischer Autorisierung

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.claim: The first stanza is symmetrical, with matching behavior-to-consequence sequences and a cross-rhyme produced by vowel variation, as Neuwirth observes.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.anchor: Die symmetrische Binnengliederung des Gesätzes in eine zweimalige Durchführung des Schemas ‚diesseitiges Verhalten – jenseitige Konsequenz’ unterstreicht ein durch Vokalvariation erzielter Kreuzreimeffekt

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.claim: The two halves are linked by paired terms: giving versus stinginess, piety versus self-sufficiency, affirmation versus denial, and ease versus hardship.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.anchor: V. 5 und 8 sind durch die Verwendung von Antonymen aufeinander bezogen: ʾaʿtā, „geben“ vs. baḫila, „geizen“, ittaqā, „gottesfürchtig sein“ vs. istaġnā

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.claim: Neuwirth classifies verse 11 with the theological predication in verses 12–13 rather than with the preceding description of the wicked.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.anchor: anders Neuwirth, Studien, 229 und Neuwirth, Frühmekkanische Suren, 228

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

TABRISI:92:5-15/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:5-15/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:5-15/r10.claim: The miser seeks self-sufficiency by withholding God's due, or behaves as if he needs neither God nor His mercy.

THALABI:v10p217/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء عن النبي
THALABI:v10p217/r1.claim: At each sunset two angels call out for all creatures except humans and jinn: God should repay the spender and destroy the hoarder; the passage was revealed about this contrast.
THALABI:v10p217/r1.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما من يوم غربت شمسه إلا

THALABI:v10p217/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p217/r7.claim: The miser withholds good spending, acts as if independent of God and denies the promised good; God then turns him toward disapproved deeds and punishment, with al-ʿusrā also understood as Hell itself.
THALABI:v10p217/r7.anchor: وأما من بخل بالنفقة في الخير واستغنى عن ربه فلم يرغب في ثوابه وكذب بالحسنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r1.claim: Bukhila means withholding spending on good works and charity; istaghna means feeling no need for God's reward and not desiring it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r1.anchor: أي بالنفقة في الخير والصدقة (¬6) {واستغنى} عن ثواب الله فلم يرغب فيه (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r2.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r2.claim: They identify the person as Abu Sufyan, then generalize the warning to disbelievers after him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل (¬1)، والكلبي (¬2): يعني أبا سفيان، ثم عمت الكفار بعده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r3.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r3.claim: He identifies the person as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p80/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء: يريد أمية بن خلف (¬3)

WAHIDI-QT:92:8/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:8/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:8/r1.claim: The miser withholds spending for good, considers himself independent of God, and does not seek His reward.
WAHIDI-QT:92:8/r1.anchor: بالنفقة في الخير { واستغنى } عن الله فلم يرغب في ثوابه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:8/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:8/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:8/r1.claim: The miser withholds spending for good and considers himself independent of God, without hoping for His reward.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:8/r1.anchor: { وأما من بخل } بالنفقة في الخير { واستغنى } عن الله، فلم يرغب في ثوابه.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.claim: The givers seek the Hereafter, while misers seek worldly life; both the first and last life belong to God, so people should follow His guidance in each.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.anchor: لأن الذي يعطي ويتقي يريد الآخرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.claim: The lām emphasizing God's ownership suits the surah's repeated focus on wealth and possession; unlike this context, the wealth-free context of 53:25 omits it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.anchor: فسياق الآيات في سورة الليل جاء كله في الأموال وامتلاكها والتصرف فيها

ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r5.claim: The miser withholds wealth and avoids paying what is due.

ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r6.claim: Istighnā means imagining oneself already self-sufficient, free of future need and protection, and absorbed in one's present self, wealth, and worldly desires.
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r6.anchor: kendini gınâya ermiş, en güzel âkıbeti bulmuş, ilerisi için hiçbir ihtiyâcı kalmamış, artık korunmaktan vâreste olmuş ganî addederek hâline, ferdiyetine saplanmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r3.claim: The surah presents two character types: the generous, self-giving Muslim and, by implication, the miserly, selfish disbeliever.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:5/r3.anchor: bunlardan ilki olan cömert ve özverili tip müslüman insanı, cimri ve bencil tip de inkârcıyı temsil etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r1.claim: The miser's claim of sufficiency means trusting his own power and possessions so arrogantly that he sees himself as needing nothing, even before God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r1.anchor: kendi gücüne ve elindekilere güvenip Allah karşısında bile kendisini ihtiyaçsız görecek kadar kibirde ileri giden kişinin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

THALABI:v10p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r1.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p220/r1.claim: A man refused the Prophet’s offer of a date palm in Paradise for his palm that dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard; Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought and donated it, and the Prophet transferred it to the neighbor. The account identifies them with the surah’s contrasting figures.
THALABI:v10p220/r1.anchor: عطاء قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، وكان له جار، فكان يسقط من بلحها في دار جاره

THALABI:v10p220/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p220/r3.claim: The palm’s owner represents the miser who deems himself self-sufficient and denies reward; he is eased toward Hell and is the “most wretched” who enters the blazing fire.
THALABI:v10p220/r3.anchor: وأما من بخل واستغنى يعني الأنصاري وكذب بالحسنى يعني الثواب فسنيسره للعسرى يعني النار

TAB:92:8/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:8/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:8/r1.claim: The miser withholds God's bestowed wealth from required spending and acts as self-sufficient from his Lord, failing to seek Him through obedience or increased giving.
TAB:92:8/r1.anchor: من صرفه في الوجوه التي أمر الله بصرفه فيها

TAB:92:8/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:8/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:92:8/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says he withholds what he has and considers himself self-sufficient; another wording says he withholds bounty and feels independent of his Lord.
TAB:92:8/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   في قوله :  وأما من بخل واستغنى قال :  بخل بما عنده

TAB:92:8/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:8/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:92:8/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains this as a person enriched by God who withholds the zakat due.
TAB:92:8/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس وأما من بخل واستغنى يقول :  من أغناه الله ،  فبخل بالزكاة

TAB:92:8/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:8/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:92:8/r4.claim: Qatada says this is one who withholds God's due and feels inwardly independent of his Lord.
TAB:92:8/r4.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله وأما من بخل واستغنى :  وأما من بخل بحق الله عليه

BURHAN:v3p209/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p209/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p209/r4.claim: Deleting a conjunction can make coordinated clauses feel like one, as in the omitted waw before do not spare you harm, and in the cited faces and Tabuk passages.
BURHAN:v3p209/r4.anchor: فمنه الواو تحذف لقصد البلاغة فإن في إثباتها ما يقتضى تغاير المتعاطفين

ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r1.claim: The contrast pairs giving with stinginess and piety with self-sufficiency: the miser disregards what God has and claims not to need it.
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r1.anchor: وقابل أعطى ببخل ، واتقى باستغنى ، لأنه زهد فيما عند الله بقوله : { واستغنى }

ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God abandons the miser and withholds grace until obedience becomes hardest, citing the constricted heart; the author flags this opening explanation as Muʿtazilī.
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : فسنخذله ونمنعه الألطاف حتى تكون الطاعة أعسر شيء عليه وأشد كقوله : { يجعل صدره ضيقاً حرجاً كأنما يصعد في السماء }

ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī alternatively says the paths are named for their outcomes, ease and hardship, or means the paths to Paradise and Hell in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r4.anchor: إذ سمى طريقة الخير باليسرى لأن عاقبتها اليسر ، وطريقة الشر العسرى لأن عاقبتها العسر ، أو أراد بهما طريقي الجنة والنار

ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r5.claim: The author marks al-Zamakhsharī’s account of withholding divine grace as carrying a Muʿtazilī insinuation.

ALUSI:92:8/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:8/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:8/r1.claim: He withholds his wealth instead of spending it in good causes.
ALUSI:92:8/r1.anchor: بما له فلم يبذله في سبيل الخير

ALUSI:92:8/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:8/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:8/r2.claim: A reported alternative says he withholds obedience to what he was commanded; al-Alūsī dismisses it.
ALUSI:92:8/r2.anchor: وقيل أي بخل بفعل ما أمر به وفيه ما فيه

ALUSI:92:8/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:8/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:8/r3.claim: He behaves as though he has no need of God or what is with Him, and so does not fear Him.
ALUSI:92:8/r3.anchor: وزهد فيما عنده عز وجل كأنه مستغن عنه سبحانه فلم يتقه

ALUSI:92:8/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:8/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:8/r4.claim: Alternatively he is satisfied with worldly desires instead of afterlife bliss, fitting the contrast with God-consciousness.
ALUSI:92:8/r4.anchor: أو استغنى بشهوات الدنيا عن نعيم العقبى

ALUSI:92:8/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:8/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:8/r5.claim: The comparison to al-ḥusnā follows the interpretations already given for verse 6.
ALUSI:92:8/r5.anchor: والمراد بالحسنى فيه ما مر في الأقوال قبل

ALUSI:92:10/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r5.speaker: الإرشاد
ALUSI:92:10/r5.claim: Al-Irshād says giving and withholding head the two clauses, though lower in rank than what follows, because each is foundational to the ensuing faith and piety or denial and self-sufficiency.
ALUSI:92:10/r5.anchor: لعل تصدير القسمين بالإعطاء والبخل مع أن كلا منهما أدنى رتبة مما بعد

ALUSI:92:10/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r11.claim: Despite specific reported occasions, the two descriptions apply generally because the wording is general; each person named is an included example.
ALUSI:92:10/r11.anchor: وان كان السبب خاصاً إذ العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب نعم هو قطعي الدخول

ALUSI:92:10/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r12.claim: One view identifies the giver as Abū Bakr and the miser as Umayya b. Khalaf.
ALUSI:92:10/r12.anchor: وقيل من أعطى أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه ومن بخل أمية بن خلف

ALUSI:92:10/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:92:10/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to identify them as Abū Bakr and Abū Sufyān b. Ḥarb; al-Alūsī questions this because Abū Sufyān later became a strong Muslim according to Sunnis.
ALUSI:92:10/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن الأول أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه والثاني أبو سفيان بن حرب

ALUSI:92:10/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r14.speaker: الطستي
ALUSI:92:10/r14.claim: In al-Ṭustī's narration from Ibn ʿAbbās, the miser passage was revealed about Abū Jahl; al-Alūsī treats all named identities as instances of the general wording.

BAGHAWI:92:8/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:8/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:8/r1.claim: The miser withholds charitable spending, considers himself independent of God's reward, and does not seek it.
BAGHAWI:92:8/r1.anchor: { وأما من بخل } بالنفقة في الخير ،   { واستغنى } عن ثواب الله فلم يرغب فيه

BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.claim: An anonymous report says the passage was revealed about Abu Bakr buying Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf for a garment and ten coins and freeing him; their opposed efforts are contrasted.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.anchor: قيل : نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق اشترى بلالاً من أمية ابن خلف ببردة وعشرة أوراق ،   فأعتقه

BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.claim: Ata recounts an Ansari's palm tree whose fallen dates entered a neighbor's home; the Prophet offered a tree in Paradise, the owner refused, and Abu al-Dahdah bought it with his garden and gave it to the neighbor. The report maps the giver to Abu al-Dahdah and the miser to the Ansari.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.anchor: عن عطاء ،   قال : " كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة وكان له جار يسقط من بلحها في داره

BAYDAWI:92:8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:8/r1.claim: The miser withholds what was commanded and treats worldly desires as sufficient in place of the bliss of the afterlife.
BAYDAWI:92:8/r1.anchor: بما أمر به واستغنى بشهوات الدنيا عن نعيم العقبى

BIQAI:92:8/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:8/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:8/r1.claim: After describing the one who purifies himself and that person's reward, the passage turns to the one who corrupts himself and his wretched fate.
BIQAI:92:8/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر المزكي وثمرته ،   أتبعه المدسي وشقوته

BIQAI:92:8/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:8/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:8/r2.claim: The miser withholds what God commanded or encouraged him to give; he seeks independence from people and from promised reward, trusting deluded hopes, so he neither benefits people nor works for the afterlife.
BIQAI:92:8/r2.anchor: فمنع ما أمر به وندب إليه

DURR:92:5/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:5/r3.claim: In the report through ʿIkrima, Ibn Abbas says the miser withholds his wealth and considers himself independent of his Lord.
DURR:92:5/r3.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى } من الفضل { واتقى } قال : اتقى ربه

DURR:92:5/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:92:5/r6.claim: Qatada says the miser withholds God's due, feels independent of his Lord, and denies God's promised reward.
DURR:92:5/r6.anchor: عن قتادة { فأما من أعطى } قال : أعطى حق الله عليه { واتقى } محارم الله

DURR:92:5/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:5/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says affirming the good means belief in monotheism, and says the miser is one whom God enriched but who withheld zakat.
DURR:92:5/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس { وصدق بالحسنى } يقول صدق بلا إله ألا الله { وأما من بخل واستغنى } يقول : من أغناه الله فبخل بالزكاة

DURR:92:5/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:5/r13.claim: In a report through al-Kalbi and Abu Salih, Ibn Abbas identifies the giver as Abu Bakr and the miser who denies the good as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
DURR:92:5/r13.anchor: في طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى فسنيسره لليسرى } قال : أبو بكر الصديق

DURR:92:5/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR:92:5/r14.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise and Hell is written, yet commanded action: people are facilitated toward deeds of felicity or misery, then he recited these verses.
DURR:92:5/r14.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : «كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة فقال : ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد كتب مقعده من الجنة ومقعده من النار

DURR:92:5/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r15.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
DURR:92:5/r15.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami reports that after 54:49 was revealed, a man asked whether deeds were newly begun or already decreed; the Prophet replied to act, since each is facilitated toward ease or hardship.
DURR:92:5/r15.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية { إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر } [ القمر : 49 ] قال رجل : يا رسول الله ففيم العمل

DURR:92:6/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:6/r3.claim: In the report through ʿIkrima, Ibn Abbas says the miser withholds his wealth and considers himself independent of his Lord.

DURR:92:6/r6.anchor: عن قتادة { فأما من أعطى } قال : أعطى حق الله عليه { واتقى } محارم الله

DURR:92:7/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:92:7/r6.claim: Qatada says the miser withholds God's due, feels independent of his Lord, and denies God's promised reward.
DURR:92:7/r6.anchor: عن قتادة { فأما من أعطى } قال : أعطى حق الله عليه { واتقى } محارم الله

DURR:92:7/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:7/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:7/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says affirming the good means belief in monotheism, and says the miser is one whom God enriched but who withheld zakat.
DURR:92:7/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس { وصدق بالحسنى } يقول صدق بلا إله ألا الله { وأما من بخل واستغنى } يقول : من أغناه الله فبخل بالزكاة

DURR:92:7/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:7/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:7/r13.claim: In a report through al-Kalbi and Abu Salih, Ibn Abbas identifies the giver as Abu Bakr and the miser who denies the good as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
DURR:92:7/r13.anchor: في طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى فسنيسره لليسرى } قال : أبو بكر الصديق

DURR:92:7/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:7/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR:92:7/r14.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise and Hell is written, yet commanded action: people are facilitated toward deeds of felicity or misery, then he recited these verses.
DURR:92:7/r14.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : «كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة فقال : ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد كتب مقعده من الجنة ومقعده من النار

DURR:92:7/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:7/r15.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
DURR:92:7/r15.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami reports that after 54:49 was revealed, a man asked whether deeds were newly begun or already decreed; the Prophet replied to act, since each is facilitated toward ease or hardship.
DURR:92:7/r15.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية { إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر } [ القمر : 49 ] قال رجل : يا رسول الله ففيم العمل

DURR:92:8/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:8/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:8/r3.claim: In the report through ʿIkrima, Ibn Abbas says the miser withholds his wealth and considers himself independent of his Lord.
DURR:92:8/r3.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى } من الفضل { واتقى } قال : اتقى ربه

DURR:92:8/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:8/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:92:8/r6.claim: Qatada says the miser withholds God's due, feels independent of his Lord, and denies God's promised reward.
DURR:92:8/r6.anchor: عن قتادة { فأما من أعطى } قال : أعطى حق الله عليه { واتقى } محارم الله

DURR:92:8/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:8/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:8/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says affirming the good means belief in monotheism, and says the miser is one whom God enriched but who withheld zakat.
DURR:92:8/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس { وصدق بالحسنى } يقول صدق بلا إله ألا الله { وأما من بخل واستغنى } يقول : من أغناه الله فبخل بالزكاة

DURR:92:8/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:8/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:8/r13.claim: In a report through al-Kalbi and Abu Salih, Ibn Abbas identifies the giver as Abu Bakr and the miser who denies the good as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
DURR:92:8/r13.anchor: في طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى فسنيسره لليسرى } قال : أبو بكر الصديق

DURR:92:8/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:8/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR:92:8/r14.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise and Hell is written, yet commanded action: people are facilitated toward deeds of felicity or misery, then he recited these verses.
DURR:92:8/r14.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : «كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة فقال : ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد كتب مقعده من الجنة ومقعده من النار

DURR:92:8/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:8/r15.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
DURR:92:8/r15.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami reports that after 54:49 was revealed, a man asked whether deeds were newly begun or already decreed; the Prophet replied to act, since each is facilitated toward ease or hardship.
DURR:92:8/r15.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية { إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر } [ القمر : 49 ] قال رجل : يا رسول الله ففيم العمل

IBNASHUR:92:5/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r6.claim: The two main groups may be those enabled toward ease and those toward hardship, encompassing different deeds and serving exhortation and warning.
IBNASHUR:92:5/r6.anchor: فريق ميسر لليسرى وفريق ميسر للعسرى

IBNASHUR:92:5/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r7.claim: The division is also illustrated by the day people emerge separately to see their deeds, including outcomes of even the smallest good or evil.
IBNASHUR:92:5/r7.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { يومئذٍ يصدر الناس أشتاتاً ليروا أعمالهم

IBNASHUR:92:5/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r8.claim: Alternatively, the groups are the two sets of three traits stated in verses 5 and 8–9, a valid division of varied striving.
IBNASHUR:92:5/r8.anchor: واتّقى وصدّق بالحسنى ، ومنْ بخل واستغنى وكذب بالحسنى

IBNASHUR:92:5/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r17.claim: The object of ‘was miserly’ is omitted because the intended miserliness is with wealth.
IBNASHUR:92:5/r17.anchor: لم يذكر متعلقه لأنه أريد به البخل بالمال

IBNASHUR:92:5/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r18.claim: Istighnā is set against God-consciousness: the persistent unbeliever considers himself independent of obeying God and His call, relying on idols and his people.
IBNASHUR:92:5/r18.anchor: فالمراد به الاستغناء عن امتثال أمر الله ودعوته

IBNASHUR:92:5/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r19.claim: One analysis takes the augmentative sīn and tāʾ as intensifying the action, as with istajāba (‘answered’).
IBNASHUR:92:5/r19.anchor: فالسين والتاء للمبالغة في الفعل مثل سين استحباب بمعنى أجاب

IBNASHUR:92:5/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r20.claim: Alternatively, the augmentative letters mark seeking: the person seeks greater wealth through miserliness.
IBNASHUR:92:5/r20.anchor: وقد يراد به زيادة طلب الغنى بالبخل بالمال ، فتكون السين والتاء للطلب

IBNASHUR:92:5/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r21.claim: Together, the three traits characterize a polytheist.
IBNASHUR:92:5/r21.anchor: وهذه الخلال كناية عن كونه من المشركين

IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Hell is recorded; when asked whether to rely on this, he said to act, since each is facilitated, then recited al-Layl 92:5–10.
IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان في جنازة فأخذ عودا ينكت في الأرض

IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Hell is recorded; when asked whether to rely on this, he said to act, since each is facilitated, then recited al-Layl 92:5–10.
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان في جنازة فأخذ عودا ينكت في الأرض

IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.speaker: شعبة
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.claim: Shuʿba adds that Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir also narrated the report to him, corroborating its transmission from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash.
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.anchor: قال شعبة حدثني منصور بن المعتمر فلم أنكره من حديث سليمان

IBNATIYYA:92:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:8/r1.claim: For intensified blame, construe miserliness as withholding wealth and istighnāʾ as considering oneself financially independent as well.
IBNATIYYA:92:8/r1.anchor: ولا بد من جعل بخل في المال خاصة جعل استغنى في المال أيضا لتعظم المذمة

IBNATIYYA:92:8/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:8/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:8/r2.claim: On the broader reading of miserliness as withholding anything due in words or deeds, istighnāʾ means claiming to need neither God nor His mercy.
IBNATIYYA:92:8/r2.anchor: ومن جعل البخل عاما في جميع ما ينبغي أن يبذل من قول وفعل قال استغنى عن الله ورحمته

IBNKATHIR:92:7/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:7/r3.speaker: بعض السلف
IBNKATHIR:92:7/r3.claim: Some early authorities say one reward of a good deed is the good deed that follows, and one punishment of sin is the sin that follows; Ibn Kathir links this to the next clause.
IBNKATHIR:92:7/r3.anchor: وقال بعض السلف : من ثواب الحسنة

IBNKATHIR:92:8/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:8/r1.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:92:8/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, as relayed by ʿIkrima, explains that the person withholds his wealth and considers himself independent of his Lord.
IBNKATHIR:92:8/r1.anchor: قال عكرمة ،   عن ابن عباس : أي بخل بماله ،   واستغنى عن ربه ،   عز وجل

KASHSHAF:92:8/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:8/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:8/r1.claim: He may disdain what is with God as though he does not need it, and so fail to fear God.
KASHSHAF:92:8/r1.anchor: وزهد فيما عند الله كأنه مستغن عنه فلم يتقه

KASHSHAF:92:8/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:8/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:8/r2.claim: Or he treats worldly desires as sufficient in place of Paradise's delights, the contrast to “he was God-fearing.”
KASHSHAF:92:8/r2.anchor: عن نعيم الجنة ،   لأنه في مقابلة

KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.claim: A report says these verses were revealed concerning Abū Bakr and Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb.
KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.anchor: نزلتا في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه

MAWARDI:92:8/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:8/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI:92:8/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd identifies the miserly, self-sufficient people as Umayya and Ubayy, the sons of Khalaf.
MAWARDI:92:8/r1.anchor:
قال ابن مسعود : يعني بذلك
أمية وأبياً ابني خلف .

MAWARDI:92:8/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:8/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
MAWARDI:92:8/r2.claim: Being miserly means withholding one's wealth, which will not last.
MAWARDI:92:8/r2.anchor: أحدهما : بخل بماله الذي لا يبقى ،   قاله ابن عباس والحسن

MAWARDI:92:8/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:8/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:92:8/r3.claim: Alternatively, it means withholding God's due.
MAWARDI:92:8/r3.anchor: الثاني : بخل بحق الله تعالى ،   قاله قتادة

MAWARDI:92:8/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:8/r4.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:92:8/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes self-sufficiency as relying on one's wealth.

MAWARDI:92:8/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:8/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:92:8/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes it as feeling independent of one's Lord.
MAWARDI:92:8/r5.anchor: الثاني : عن ربه ،   قاله ابن عباس

NASAFI:92:8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:8/r1.claim: He is miserly with his wealth.
NASAFI:92:8/r1.anchor: { وَأَمَّا مَن بَخِلَ } بماله { واستغنى } عن ربه فلم يتقه

NASAFI:92:8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:8/r2.claim: He may regard himself as independent of his Lord and so not fear Him.

NASAFI:92:8/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:8/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:8/r3.claim: Alternatively, he is absorbed in worldly desires instead of the bliss of the afterlife.
NASAFI:92:8/r3.anchor: أو استغنى بشهوات الدنيا عن نعيم العقبى

QURTUBI:92:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:8/r1.claim: The miser clings to what he has and gives no good; his worldly outcome was discussed in Al Imran, while his hereafter is the Fire.
QURTUBI:92:8/r1.anchor: أي ضن بما عنده ، فلم يبذل خيرا

QURTUBI:92:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:8/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:92:8/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf.
QURTUBI:92:8/r3.anchor: وعنه عن ابن عباس قال : نزلت في أمية بن خلف

QURTUBI:92:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:8/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
QURTUBI:92:8/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Ikrima, explains that the person hoarded his wealth and considered himself independent of his Lord.
QURTUBI:92:8/r4.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس : " وأما من بخل واستغنى " يقول : بخل بماله

RAZI:92:1/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:1/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:1/r2.claim: Despite that reported occasion, the sūra’s meaning is general, as its statements that human striving differs and that a blazing fire is warned of show.
RAZI:92:1/r2.anchor: إلا أنها وإن كانت كذلك لكن معانيها عامة للناس

RAZI:92:5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:5/r1.claim: The paired descriptions explain how differing deeds lead to good or bad outcomes, reward or punishment.
RAZI:92:5/r1.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه بين معنى اختلاف الأعمال فيما قلناه من العاقبة المحمودة
